data.title: Crack the Motion Vault
data.statement:
A mysterious vault is controlled by a motion device.

Instead of entering a password, the user performs physical gestures. The device sends raw hexadecimal packets containing gyroscope and accelerometer readings.

Your task is to decode the packets and reconstruct the gesture password.

<<Packet format>>

Each packet consists of exactly {{14}} bytes, represented by two-digit uppercase hexadecimal values separated by spaces.

{{22 00}} [[gx]] [[gy]] [[gz]] [[ax]] [[ay]] [[az]]

The first two bytes, {{22 00}}, form the fixed header.

Each of [[gx]], [[gy]], [[gz]], [[ax]], [[ay]], and [[az]] represents two bytes. These are six signed 16-bit integers encoded in little-endian order using two's complement representation.

- [[gx]], [[gy]], [[gz]]: gyroscope readings for the X, Y, and Z axes.
- [[ax]], [[ay]], [[az]]: accelerometer readings for the X, Y, and Z axes.

Examples of little-endian two's complement decoding:

- {{01 00}} represents {{1}}.
- {{FF 7F}} represents {{32767}}.
- {{FF FF}} represents {{-1}}.
- {{00 80}} represents {{-32768}}.

<<Gesture detection>>

For each packet, calculate [[G]] as the largest absolute value among the three gyroscope readings.

Calculate [[A]] by adding together the absolute values of the three accelerometer readings.

A packet represents a valid gesture only when [[G]] ≥ {{400}} and [[A]] ≥ {{3000}}.

Otherwise, ignore the packet.

<<Gesture direction>>

For each valid packet, find the gyroscope axis with the greatest absolute value.

If multiple axes are tied, prioritize X, then Y, then Z.

Convert the dominant axis into a character based on its sign:

- Positive X: {{R}} (Right)
- Negative X: {{L}} (Left)
- Positive Y: {{U}} (Up)
- Negative Y: {{D}} (Down)
- Positive Z: {{F}} (Forward)
- Negative Z: {{B}} (Backward)

<<Duplicate filtering>>

The device may transmit multiple packets for the same gesture.

Append a gesture character to the password only if it differs from the last accepted gesture.

Ignored packets do not reset the previous accepted gesture.

For example, {{R R U U R F F}} becomes {{RURF}}.
data.constraints:
{{1}} ≤ [[N]] ≤ {{10}}

Each sensor reading ([[gx]], [[gy]], [[gz]], [[ax]], [[ay]], [[az]]) is between {{-32768}} and {{32767}}, inclusive.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

A mysterious vault is controlled by a motion device.

Instead of entering a password, the user performs physical gestures. The device sends raw hexadecimal packets containing gyroscope and accelerometer readings.

Your task is to decode the packets and reconstruct the gesture password.

Packet format

Each packet consists of exactly 14 bytes, represented by two-digit uppercase hexadecimal values separated by spaces.

22 00 gx gy gz ax ay az

The first two bytes, 22 00, form the fixed header.

Each of gx, gy, gz, ax, ay, and az represents two bytes. These are six signed 16-bit integers encoded in little-endian order using two's complement representation.

- gx, gy, gz: gyroscope readings for the X, Y, and Z axes.
- ax, ay, az: accelerometer readings for the X, Y, and Z axes.

Examples of little-endian two's complement decoding:

- 01 00 represents 1.
- FF 7F represents 32767.
- FF FF represents -1.
- 00 80 represents -32768.

Gesture detection

For each packet, calculate G as the largest absolute value among the three gyroscope readings.

Calculate A by adding together the absolute values of the three accelerometer readings.

A packet represents a valid gesture only when G ≥ 400 and A ≥ 3000.

Otherwise, ignore the packet.

Gesture direction

For each valid packet, find the gyroscope axis with the greatest absolute value.

If multiple axes are tied, prioritize X, then Y, then Z.

Convert the dominant axis into a character based on its sign:

- Positive X: R (Right)
- Negative X: L (Left)
- Positive Y: U (Up)
- Negative Y: D (Down)
- Positive Z: F (Forward)
- Negative Z: B (Backward)

Duplicate filtering

The device may transmit multiple packets for the same gesture.

Append a gesture character to the password only if it differs from the last accepted gesture.

Ignored packets do not reset the previous accepted gesture.

For example, R R U U R F F becomes RURF.
Input
Line 1: An integer N, the number of motion packets.

Next N lines: Each line contains exactly 14 space-separated, two-digit hexadecimal bytes. All hexadecimal letters are uppercase (A through F).
Output
Line 1: The decoded gesture password, consisting of the characters R, L, U, D, F, or B, with consecutive duplicate gestures removed.

If no valid gestures are detected, output LOCKED.
Constraints
1 ≤ N ≤ 10

Each sensor reading (gx, gy, gz, ax, ay, az) is between -32768 and 32767, inclusive.
Example
Input
3
22 00 F4 01 00 00 00 00 D0 07 E8 03 00 00
22 00 00 00 58 02 00 00 00 00 18 FC A0 F6
22 00 00 00 00 00 E0 FC 18 FC 18 FC 24 FA
Output
RUB
